items.title: [Feature]: Expose CPU vs P2P attribution for multi-tier KV restores
items.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`TieringOffloadingSpec` does not expose whether restored prompt KV came from its CPU primary tier or its P2P secondary tier.

The available metrics collapse the two paths:

- `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source_total{source="external_kv_transfer"}` includes every external KV source.
- `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` and `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries_total` have no source label.
- `vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total` has no tier label.
- The P2P secondary tier emits no transfer counters.
- NIXL transfer metrics have no connector or tier label.

`kv_offload_load_bytes_total` is not a proxy for CPU-cache hits. A P2P promotion lands in the CPU primary tier before the CPU-to-GPU load, so P2P restores also contribute to that counter.

I think we need two separate measurements.

First, attribute restored prompt tokens to the tier that satisfied the lookup:

```
vllm:external_prompt_tokens_by_source_total{source="cpu"}
vllm:external_prompt_tokens_by_source_total{source="p2p"}
```

`cpu` means the primary tier satisfied the blocks without promotion. `p2p` means the primary tier missed and `P2PSecondaryTierManager` supplied them.

Second, expose transfer volume for each physical tier:

```
vllm:kv_offload_tier_load_bytes_total{tier="cpu"}
vllm:kv_offload_tier_load_bytes_total{tier="p2p"}
vllm:kv_offload_tier_load_blocks_total{tier="cpu"}
vllm:kv_offload_tier_load_blocks_total{tier="p2p"}
```

The names are examples. Existing `external_kv_transfer` aggregates should remain valid. Labels should identify bounded tier types rather than peer IDs.

Related issues:

- #33289 implemented the combined prompt-token source metric and lists `cache_source`/`kv_source` labels as future work.
- #38260 defines the CPU-primary/secondary-tier architecture.
- #53083 notes that the P2P tier emits no metrics, but tracks a separate protocol-correctness problem.

### Alternatives

`external - CPU` is not valid: external reuse is measured in prompt tokens, while offload counters measure bytes on a hop that both CPU hits and P2P promotions traverse. Pod network counters also include unrelated traffic and do not identify successful KV reuse.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched relevant open and closed issues. #33289 is the closest issue, but it is closed and leaves CPU/P2P attribution as future work.

items.title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Support pipeline-parallel producers on the pull path (incl. hybrid-Mamba)
items.body:
## Purpose

Lift the two `NotImplementedError` guards that block NIXL **pull-mode** disaggregation when the producer (prefill) runs with `pipeline_parallel_size > 1`:

1. the `kv_consumer` × `pp_size > 1` guard in the shared `NixlBaseConnectorWorker` constructor, and
2. the `pp_size > 1` × hybrid-KV (HMA) guard.

Successor of #48263 (draft, written against the pre-package single-file connector): the connector became a package and main absorbed that PR's foundation (per-`(pp_rank, tp_rank)` remote agents, multi-stage handshake, SSM-aware descriptor split), so this PR re-lands only the still-missing pull-path half, re-authored for the current architecture. I will close #48263 in favour of this PR.

**Not duplicating the open push-path PP work.** #50494 (`region_members` for attention-HMA PP push), #47981 (attention-HMA PP push prefill), #51053 (Kimi KDA+MLA members, stacked on #50494) and #50499 (packed MLA PP push) all extend `NixlPushConnectorWorker`. This PR touches the **pull** (READ) worker; the two modes are protocol-incompatible and separated in the compatibility hash by `transfer_mode`. Push semantics are unchanged here and the push guards keep raising.

One deliberate overlap to flag for reviewers: #50494 introduces a `NixlAgentMetadata.region_members` field with the same name and the same intent (per-region dedup'd member names) for the push path. This PR adds the field for the pull path. Whichever lands first should own the field; I am happy to rebase onto #50494's version and drop mine — the pull-side consumer logic here is orthogonal to how the producer advertises members.

**Commit 1 — pipeline-parallel producers on the pull path (no-HMA).**
The consumer completes one handshake per producer stage, keeps per-shard transfer handles and per-stage `TransferTopology` plans keyed by `(engine_id, pp_rank)`, and issues one read per producer stage against that stage's advertised regions (resolved via `registered_layer_names`). The constructor guard becomes a `_supports_consumer_pp` class flag: `True` on the pull worker, unchanged (raise) on push.

**Commit 2 — hybrid-Mamba (HMA) producers under PP.**
HMA pools several KV groups into one backing tensor; registration dedups by base address, so a pooled region is advertised under one representative layer name. A PP producer registers only its own layer slice, and a consumer that resolves that slice by representative names alone silently omits every non-representative member. With a hybrid model the Mamba members are exactly the ones dropped, so decode returns coherent-but-stale output instead of failing. The producer now records the dedup'd member names per region (`region_members`) and the consumer emits descriptors per (region × member-group) plus the Mamba conv/ssm section per stage, mirroring the whole-engine layout at shard scope.

Still raising by design: hetero-TP × HMA × PP; a PP consumer with HMA reading a PP=1 producer; a PP producer that advertises no `registered_layer_names`; and push-mode PP consumers.

Interop: a stock PP=1 peer omits `registered_layer_names`/`region_members` (msgspec defaults) and takes the untouched whole-engine path. `NIXL_CONNECTOR_VERSION` bumps **9 → 10** (one bump for the series); `pp_size` stays out of the compatibility hash.

## Test Plan

Unit, no GPU, via `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_pp.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ -q
pre-commit run --all-files
```

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_pp.py` is new (25 cases): per-stage handshake and read accounting, shard-relative descriptor ids, per-(region × member-group) emission, the Mamba section and its stride (Mamba1/Mamba2 parametrized), empty-group skipping, `region_members` round-trip plus rejection of a partial advertisement, pooled-member resolution, compat-hash `pp_size`-invariance, and the guard narrowing (pull allows, push still raises).

## Test Result

**Unit.** 25/25 new cases pass on this branch. Negative controls: the 14 commit-1 cases were run on stock `main` (10 failed / 4 passed — the 4 passers exercise PP scaffolding main already has), and the 11 commit-2 cases on the commit-1 parent (11 failed / 14 passed). Full `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/`: **312 failed / 846 passed / 27 skipped / 92 errors** on this branch vs **312 failed / 821 passed / 27 skipped / 92 errors** on stock `main` — the failing/erroring set is identical (404 ids, diffed both directions), all pre-existing in a GPU-less environment; passes go 821 → 846. `ruff check` clean, `ruff format --diff` clean.

**End-to-end**, 4× B200 (HyperPod EKS, EFA/libfabric NIXL backend), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B (hybrid Mamba), Dynamo disagg pull mode, prefill **TP8/PP2** (2 nodes) → decode TP8/PP1, 2026-08-22:

- Stock: deterministic `NotImplementedError` in the shared worker constructor — the guard this PR lifts. Patched: all 4 pods Ready, 0 restarts over ~31 min, prefill `Worker_PP0`/`Worker_PP1` both serving.
- Decode NIXL telemetry reads **both** producer stages at byte parity: PP2 = 16 transfers × 30.41 MB, PP1 reference = 8 × 60.82 MB, **486.56 MB per request either way** (16 = 2 stages × 8 decode ranks). Per-stage transfer plans logged for `remote_pp=0` and `remote_pp=1`. So the stages tile the model exactly once, which is the discriminator for the dropped-member bug commit 2 fixes.
- Output vs the PP1/PP1 reference run at temperature 0: prompt A byte-identical across all 48 tokens; prompt B identical for ~40 tokens then a benign synonym variation inside the reasoning block, both coherent and correct. I read that as floating-point non-determinism across a different parallel decomposition rather than stale SSM state, which presents as incoherent or wrong content, not a one-word swap — but I want to be straight that it is **not** byte-identical on every prompt.
- Scope of the hardware evidence: asymmetric PP2-prefill → PP1-decode. Symmetric PP2/PP2 (consumer-side PP with HMA) is enabled by these commits but **not yet run**, so I am not claiming it. The B200 AMI exposes no EFA `hw_counters` sysfs, so NIXL telemetry is the byte evidence rather than device counters.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these two commits onto the current connector package and to draft the tests. I reviewed every changed line, ran the unit suites and negative controls listed above, and ran the end-to-end 550B validation on hardware myself.

items.title: [ROCm][CI] Restore attention coverage after KV-cache layout refactor
items.body:
This is a follow-up to #51718, which standardized KV-cache layouts but also changed several ROCm test paths. It realigns FlexAttention tests with production and restores coverage for relevant AITER safety and MLA paths. It also avoids generating CUDA-only MLA prefill parameter matrices on ROCm, reducing collection from 2,911 to 591 cases. Together, these changes improve regression coverage while modestly reducing test resource usage.

- Build MLA prefill backend parameters positively by platform, using the CUDA backends on CUDA and `ROCM_AITER_FA` on ROCm.
- Exercise the production ROCm MLA combination by adding `ROCM_AITER_MLA` to the main backend matrix while retaining `ROCM_AITER_FA` for prefill.
- Restore FlexAttention direct-mask coverage on ROCm and retain slow-path coverage for sliding-window and non-causal attention without duplicating encoder-only execution.
- Restore the MiniMax M3 AITER multi-KV-head guard test and validate the follow-up on AITER-enabled MI355X GPUs.

items.title: TurboQuant KV cache: two observations from an sm121 evaluation: hybrid-model init failure; fp16 zero-point overflow on large value outliers
items.body:
(hybrid-model init failure; fp16 zero-point overflow on large value
outliers)**

We evaluated the TurboQuant KV-cache presets on a GB10 (sm121) against
our production NVFP4-KV recipe and hit two things worth reporting. Full
probe code, raw results, and methodology are public.¹

**1. Hybrid linear-attention models fail at engine init.**

`--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc` with a hybrid model (GDN
linear-attention layers alongside full-attention layers) fails with:

```
ValueError: Unknown TurboQuant cache dtype: 'auto'.
Valid presets: turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, turboquant_k3v4_nc, turboquant_3bit_nc
```

The state layers resolve to cache dtype `auto`, and the TurboQuant
backend has no path for a mixed-layer model. If hybrids are intended to
be unsupported, a clearer message ("hybrid models unsupported") at
config-validation time would fail earlier and clearer; if support is
intended, this is the blocker. Happy to test either on sm121.

**2. The value path's fp16 zero-point silently overflows on large
outliers (probe-level).**

`triton_turboquant_store` keeps the per-vector value scale and zero-point
in fp16 regardless of input dtype (`sc_f16` / `zr_f16`). With bf16
inputs containing an attention-sink-scale outlier of |min| > 65504, the
zero-point overflows and the reconstructed values come back as **∞** —
a poisoned cache line rather than graceful degradation. We verified this
in a model-free store→decode round-trip (single-key decode isolates the
value path): at a measured-provenance sink of ~125k the reconstruction
is ∞ for every preset; at ~42k it is finite (outliers exact, at the cost
of a coarser step for the rest of that token's vector — expected
per-vector-scale behavior). Values of this magnitude do occur in real
checkpoints (we measured v-cache sinks up to ~125k on a current 27B).

A possible mitigation: store scale/zero in fp32 (+4 bytes per vector) or
clamp with a warning. We could not confirm the overflow end to end on
our model family because of observation 1 — so this stands as a
kernel-level finding with a deterministic repro.

Repro probe (self-contained, no model needed):
https://github.com/TechPrototyper/local-ai-lab/blob/master/probes/turboquant_vs_nvfp4_value_probe.py

¹ https://github.com/TechPrototyper/local-ai-lab/blob/master/notes/turboquant-vs-nvfp4-kv-value-probe.md

items.title: [Core][KV Connector][NIXL] Defer pull posting until after model launch
items.body:
## Purpose

In scaled P/D setup, we see decode spend long host time posting NIXL pull requests: i.e. 5ms for 9 remote KV requests fanned out across TP8 (= 72 NIXL handles), occasionally spike to 48.427ms. 72 NIXL handles. 

* The time consuming part consists of synchronous descriptor construction: `make_prepped_xfer()` + `transfer()`, since the work in done synchronously in `pre_forward()` it delayed gpu model forward().

* This PR moves the NIXL request construction path to `post_forward()`, allows GPU work to overlap with the CPU side NIXL post construction. It trades TTFT for shorter TPOT.

### Duplicate-work check

The closest open work is #45211, which offloads NIXL READ submission to a dedicated reader thread and introduces cross-thread queue/locking ownership. This PR is materially different and smaller: it creates no thread and no concurrent connector-state access; posting remains synchronous on the model-runner thread but occurs after the current model forward is enqueued. Searches for deferred `start_load_kv()`/`post_forward()` ordering found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance was used for trace analysis, implementation support, tests, and preparation of this draft. The author will review the exact public diff before marking it ready for review.

## Test Plan

Tested on a two-node P/D  setup with Qwen3-0.6B, one TP1 producer and one TP1 decoder, Ran 1,319 GSM8K with concurrency 64. see 5% reduction in TPOT with 0.1% increase in TTFT.

| Metric | Control A2 | Deferred B | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | 14,471.9 ms | 14,481.5 ms | +9.6 ms (+0.07%) |
| TPOT | 4.940 ms/token | 4.697 ms/token | -0.243 ms (-4.92%) |
| ITL | 4.939 ms/token | 4.701 ms/token | -0.239 ms (-4.83%) |
| E2E | 15,077.9 ms | 15,053.3 ms | -24.6 ms (-0.16%) |

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Guard P2P supply against consumer demand
items.body:
## Purpose

Addresses #53083.

In the PD flow over the P2P secondary tier the producer's supply and the consumer's demand are computed by two independent code paths on two engines, and nothing verifies they agree. When they diverge the consumer's unmatched demand parks until `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S` and it recomputes the prompt. #52808 and #53062 are two instances of the same weakness, found separately and fixed separately.

#53083 makes the case that this needs a mechanism rather than another point fix: #51840 changed `lookup` to return `HIT_PENDING` instead of `RETRY` when it starts a promotion, and because `HIT_PENDING` keeps the consecutive-hit streak alive in `_sliding_window_lookup`, a change to lookup semantics in one file silently changed which keys the consumer demands. Nothing in the suite noticed.

This adds three declare-or-fail guards in the style of the `_SCAN_BEHAVIOR` table already on this branch, plus one diagnosability change.

**`_POLICY_KEEPS_PREFIX_HITS`** pins, per `OffloadPolicy`, whether prefix-hit chunks stay in the store path. That is the gate behind #52808: under `BLOCK_LEVEL` the scheduler sets `next_stored_chunk_idx = num_chunks` and a warm producer has nothing left to offer. A new policy has to declare. Combined with `test_on_new_request_policy` on this branch, which pins that a producer leg gets `REQUEST_LEVEL`, the chain holds: a producer leg cannot end up on a policy that skips prefix hits without one of the two failing.

**`_GROUP_STORE_PRUNING`** pins which branch of `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks` every `KVCacheSpec` resolves to. The function closes with `assert isinstance(kv_cache_spec, FullAttentionSpec)`, so it fails closed, but only at runtime on a model that uses the new type, never in CI. The test enumerates concrete `KVCacheSpec` subclasses, requires each to be declared, and drives the real function on a minimal instance.

**`test_demand_oracle_matches_a_real_lookup_scan`** pins `_demanded_keys` against a real scheduler's lookups. #53083 flags that the oracle reimplements the scan and so can drift along with production rather than pinning it, which is the #51840 failure mode. The test drives a real cold admission with every key resolving `HIT_PENDING` and asserts the keys the scheduler actually looked up are exactly the oracle's set.

The one production change is in `p2p/session/server.py`. A fetch round that ends with demand unmatched only logged counts at `debug`. It now warns and names the unmatched keys per KV cache group via `get_offload_group_idx`, so a divergence is diagnosable from one log line. In #52808 the timeout path instead printed a `PYTHONHASHSEED` hint that had nothing to do with the failure, and the reporter had to instrument a container and count chunks by hand.

### Stacking

This is stacked on #52912, whose four commits are included here. **Only `[Bugfix][KV Offload] Guard P2P supply against consumer demand` is mine.** `_demanded_keys` and `_SCAN_BEHAVIOR` are introduced by that PR, so this cannot go against `main` until it lands. Kept as a draft until then.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q
```

Each guard was mutation-checked, since a guard that cannot fail is decoration:

| mutation | expected | result |
|---|---|---|
| production stops skipping prefix hits under `BLOCK_LEVEL` | policy table fails | `FAILED ...[OffloadPolicy.BLOCK_LEVEL]` |
| a new `AttentionSpec` subclass appears | spec table fails | `FAILED ...[_NewFangledAttentionSpec]` |
| the oracle scans with the wrong window | oracle guard fails | `FAILED ...[True]` |
| the oracle drops its `[:num_chunks]` slice | oracle guard fails | `FAILED ...[True]` |

## Test Result

Run on one H100, `vllm/vllm-openai` container, source overlaid on this branch.

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering` together: 684 passed on the branch without this commit, 701 passed with it, plus the same 2 pre-existing `test_fs_tier.py` failures on both sides (they need writable paths in this container). No test changes state because of this PR.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0) pass on both changed files.

## What this does not cover

- Rows 4 and 6 of the divergence table in #53083 are examined below but not fixed here.
- The tier-level supply invariant, driven through a real `TieringOffloadingManager` rather than a `MagicMock`, is not here. That one is in #53329, where it doubles as the regression test for #53062.
- Demand-driven serving for the PD leg, raised as the long-term direction in the #52912 discussion, is a design change and deliberately out of scope.

## Following up on the divergence table

### Row 4, `prepare_store` returning None, is self-healing

On a primary allocation failure the scheduler logs and `continue`s **without** calling `advance_stored_idx`, so `next_stored_chunk_idx` stays put and the same chunks are re-offered on a later step. `advance_stored_idx` has exactly two call sites (`scheduler.py:1323` and `:1337`), neither on this path. This is the opposite shape from #53062, where the index does advance and the key is stranded. The residual exposure is only that a request can finish while primary is still full, after which nothing retries.

### Row 6 is real but narrow, and only bites through `max_offload_tokens`

The store side truncates in `_calc_num_offloadable_tokens`; the demand side starts from `max_hit_size_tokens = req_status.req.num_tokens` in `_lookup_complete_chunks` and never consults either cap. Taking the two settings separately:

- `offload_prompt_only` does not diverge. It clamps the store to `num_prompt_tokens`, and a consumer's demand at admission is over its prompt with nothing generated yet, so supply covers demand either way.
- `max_offload_tokens` does diverge. It is per-request, read from that request's own `kv_transfer_params`, and nothing propagates it from the producer leg to the consumer leg on the other engine. A producer that caps below its prompt length supplies fewer chunks than the consumer demands, and since a PD fetch round only completes when nothing is left demanded, the result is not a smaller hit but a full `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S` stall and a recompute.

That asymmetry seems worth naming: for local offloading the cap degrades gracefully, and for PD it turns into a hard failure. It is marked experimental in the code, so this may be known.

### Correction on `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`

An earlier revision of this description flagged it as reachable. **That was wrong**, and the table comment now records why. `generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` (`kv_cache_utils.py:1848`) replaces the wrapper with a representative per-layer spec before the scheduler config is built, and `EngineCore` passes that config to the connector. Only the worker side keeps the wrapper, which is exactly why `worker.py` and `canonical_mapping.py` branch on it and the scheduler path does not. It stays in the table as `None` because it is a concrete `KVCacheSpec` subclass and the exhaustiveness check demands every one be declared, not because it is a latent bug.

### `RSWASpec`: checked and cleared

An earlier revision of this description claimed R-SWA was a third instance of the
same class. **That was wrong too, and it is worth recording why so nobody
re-derives it.** Every individual link is real:

1. `RSWASpec` subclasses `FullAttentionSpec`, so the group declares no store pruning.
2. `RSWAManager.remove_skipped_blocks` frees gap blocks and replaces them with `null_block`, whose id is 0.
3. `_build_store_jobs` drops chunks whose block id is 0.
4. `RSWAManager` overrides only `remove_skipped_blocks`, so the load path scans the group as a contiguous prefix.
5. A PD consumer's `lookup` returns an unconditional `HIT`, so that scan never breaks at a hole.

What I had not checked is whether steps 2 and 3 can co-occur in time. They cannot.
A chunk becomes storable exactly when it fills, at `(i + 1) * tokens_per_chunk`
computed tokens, while R-SWA can only null block `i` once the decode window has
moved strictly past its end. Storability necessarily precedes nulling, so the
null-block filter never sees a gap chunk.

Measured on one H100 by driving a real `Scheduler` with an `RSWASpec` group and
recording, per chunk, the step it was offered to `prepare_store` against the step
its block became null. `RSWAManager` does null blocks (final block table
`[1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 7, 8]`), and every chunk is still stored first:

| config | result |
|---|---|
| `rswa_window=16`, prompt 32, decode 96 | 8/8 stored before null |
| `rswa_window=1` (fastest possible slide) | 8/8 stored before null |
| `rswa_window=1`, prompt 16, decode 160 | 11/11 stored before null |
| `rswa_window=64`, decode 240 | 16/16 stored before null |

In the `rswa_window=1` case the margin is a consistent 3 steps: chunk `i` is
offered at step `16i` and nulled at step `16i + 3`.

I also tried to invert the ordering by deferring the store, simulating a full
primary tier so `prepare_store` returns `None` for the first 40 and then 70 steps,
well past when those blocks are nulled. All 8 chunks are still stored, because
the connector's `group_state.block_ids` is captured at allocation and is not
rewritten when the scheduler nulls a block.

So R-SWA is fine, and `_GROUP_STORE_PRUNING` declaring it under the
`FullAttentionSpec` branch is correct rather than merely current behavior.

AI assistance was used for this change.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Defer request-level cascade of in-flight primary keys
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53062.

`TieringOffloadingManager._cascade_existing_blocks_to_request_level_tiers` keeps only keys whose primary-tier `lookup` is `HIT`. A `HIT_PENDING` key, present in the primary tier with its write still in flight, is dropped permanently: `prepare_store` already excluded it as present so `complete_store` never cascades it, the cascade drops it for not being readable, and the scheduler then advances `next_stored_chunk_idx` past the chunk so nothing offers it again. For a P2P producer leg nothing is parked under its `kv_request_id`, and the peer waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S` and recomputes.

The fix treats `HIT_PENDING` as "not yet" rather than "never": park those keys on the request, retry them once per step from `on_schedule_end()` next to `_flush_pending_promotions()`, and hold the request from finalization while any are parked.

The park is bounded without a timeout. `CPUOffloadingManager.complete_store(success=False)` removes the block and frees it, so a failed write resolves the key to `MISS` on the next retry; a successful one resolves it to `HIT`. Every parked key leaves the set, which is what `test_cascade_drops_deferred_keys_whose_primary_write_failed` pins. `has_pending_work()` also reports parked keys so the engine keeps ticking until they drain.

### Reachability

The cascade is currently unreachable on `main`: no secondary tier returns `OffloadPolicy.REQUEST_LEVEL`, so `request_level_tiers` is always empty. #52912 is what makes the path live for the PD producer leg. This PR is independent of it and needs no rebase, but the bug only reaches users once #52912 lands.

## Test Plan

Three tests in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py`, on the existing `manager_setup` fixture:

- `test_cascade_supply_behavior_declared_for_every_lookup_result` is the guard proposed as `_CASCADE_SUPPLY_BEHAVIOR` in #53083. A table declares `supply` / `defer` / `drop` per `LookupResult` and the test drives a real `TieringOffloadingManager` with a stubbed primary lookup, parametrized over `list(LookupResult)`, so a new member fails the suite until someone declares it.
- `test_cascade_defers_keys_whose_primary_write_is_in_flight` is the reproduction: one request leaves a GPU to primary write open, a second request-level request calls `prepare_store` on the same keys, and the peer must be offered them once the write lands.
- `test_deferred_cascade_holds_request_from_finalization` covers the request finishing while keys are still parked, which on `main` tears the secondary tiers down before the peer is ever served.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q
```

## Test Result

Run on one H100, `vllm/vllm-openai` container, source overlaid on `main`.

Both new behavioral tests fail on `main` for the right reason. `test_cascade_defers_keys_whose_primary_write_is_in_flight` fails on its substantive assertion:

```
>       assert self._cascaded_keys_for(ctx.req_id) == [set(keys)]
E       AssertionError: assert [] == [{b'0\x00\x00...x00\x00\x00'}]
E         Right contains one more item: {b'0\x00\x00\x00\x00', b'1\x00\x00\x00\x00', b'2\x00\x00\x00\x00'}
```

Before the fix: `6 failed, 1 passed`. After: `55 passed` for the file.

Wider suite, `tests/v1/kv_offload`:

| | passed | failed | errors |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `main` | 490 | 6 | 36 |
| this PR | 497 | 6 | 36 |

The 6 failures and 36 errors are identical on both sides and are environmental in this container (`test_gpu_worker.py` needs a GPU worker, `test_fs_tier.py` and the two factory tests need writable paths and dynamic module loading). No test changes state because of this PR.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (v0.14.0, the pinned pre-commit rev) pass on both changed files.

## Notes

- #53087 rewrites 103 lines of the same `tiering/manager.py` for a different bug (#49829, unbounded `HIT_PENDING` waits in `lookup()`). items.title: [KV Connector] Support MooncakeStore with hybrid DCP prefix caching
items.body:
## Purpose

This PR enables `MooncakeStoreConnector` for mamba hybrid models (e.g., kimi k3) using decode context parallelism (DCP) and fixes a bug where incorrect load keys are constructed under fine-grained prefix hits, causing KV load failures.

### Failure Example

Consider Kimi-K3 with DCP 8 + DSpark and `--prefix-match-unit 128`:

- **Attention block span under DCP:** 1,536 × 8 = 12,288 tokens
- **Mamba block span:** 1,536 tokens
- **Prefix-match unit:** 128 tokens

Reproduction steps:
1. Send a 15,000-token prompt.
2. Clear GPU local cache.
3. Send the same prompt again.

#### Cache blocks stored and keys:

| KV group | Stored state | Store-key hash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full attention | First physical block through 12,288 | `H_12288` |
| Full attention | Second physical block valid through 14,848 | `H_14848` |
| Mamba | Checkpoint at 13,824 | `H_13824` |
| Mamba | Partial state at 14,848 | `H_14848` |

#### Lookup

1. Attention matches its second physical block under `H_14848`.
3. EAGLE rewinds one 128-token unit, reducing the candidate hit length to 14,720.
4. Mamba has no checkpoint at 14,720, so it falls back to `H_13824`.
5. All groups converge to a safe `hit_length = 13,824`.

The existing load path derives the key for a group's partially reused physical block from `hit_length`. As a result, it requested `H_13824` for the attention block, even though that physical block was stored under `H_14848`. Mooncake therefore returned `-704` because the derived key did not exist.

This PR fixes this load failure by recording the precise token boundaries for partial cache store so that subsequent load requests can use the correct load key.

## Test Plan
- Mooncake store unit tests
- E2E Kimi k3 accuracy with dspark and mooncake

## Test Result
- Validated Kimi k3 DCP + dspark produces coherent results with mooncake external cache hits by clearing GPU local cache.
- Validate the same workload which causes `-704` load failure now passes with the fix.

items.title: [Docs] Document 7 undocumented kv_cache_dtype values
items.body:
## Summary

`docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md`'s `kv_cache_dtype` options list covers 3 of the 17 values `CacheDType` (`vllm/config/cache.py`) actually supports. This documents 7 of the remaining 11: `fp8_inc`, `fp8_ds_mla`, `int4_per_token_head`, `int8_per_token_head`, `fp8_per_token_head`, `nvfp4`, `nvfp4_4over6`.

Scoped to these 7 specifically because the other 4 undocumented values are the `turboquant_*` family, already the subject of the open (stalled, needs-rebase) #45422 — adding them here would collide with that PR.

## Why this doesn't duplicate an existing PR

Checked #49050 (open — despite how it's been described elsewhere, its actual diff only adds a performance section and swaps an example model, it doesn't touch this options list) and #45422 (open, TurboQuant-only, explicitly excluded from this PR's scope for that reason). Searched for any other open PR touching `quantized_kvcache.md`, `nvfp4 docs`, or `per_token_head docs` — no other open PR documents these 7 values in this file. (#48782 is an NVFP4 doc PR but touches a different file, `modelopt.md`, about ModelOpt's weight quantization, unrelated to KV-cache dtypes.)

## How each was verified

All 7 documented from source (no hardware available to verify beyond that) — grepped every implementation site for each dtype and cross-checked backend-support lists and existing docstrings against `vllm/config/cache.py`, `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`, `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/{triton_attn,flashinfer}.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/{flashmla_sparse,flashinfer_mla_sparse}.py`, `vllm/v1/attention/ops/int4_per_token_head.py`, and `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/inc.py`.

Notable corrections from an early draft, caught during review before submission:
- `fp8_inc` is not "calibrated via Intel Neural Compressor" — INC's actual code path is model-weight quantization, not KV-cache calibration. Worded to state only what's confirmed.
- `fp8_ds_mla`'s byte layout is model-specific, not universal: DeepSeek-V3.2 uses 656 bytes (512 NoPE + 16 scale + 128 RoPE), DeepSeek-V4 uses a different 584-byte layout (448 NoPE + 128 RoPE + 8 scale, different scale format). Both are now called out explicitly.
- `nvfp4`/`nvfp4_4over6` require FlashInfer's TensorRT-LLM-gen kernel path on SM100 (Blackwell datacenter GPUs) specifically, not just "the FlashInfer backend" generally.
- Added the CUDA SM89+ requirement for `fp8_per_token_head` and the power-of-two head-dimension constraint for `int4_per_token_head`'s Hadamard transform, both enforced in source but missing from the first draft.
- "per-(token, head)" corrected to "per-(token, KV head)" throughout — this is per-KV-head granularity, not per-query-head.

## Test Plan

Docs-only change, no code touched. Ran `npx markdownlint-cli2@0.21.0` (the exact version pinned in this repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) against the file with `--fix`: 0 errors, 0 changes beyond the content edit.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance (Claude) was used to research the source locations for each dtype and draft this documentation, and a second AI review pass (Codex, run independently against the live source) was used specifically to adversarially check the draft's technical claims — it caught the five corrections listed above before this was submitted. I independently re-verified each of those corrections against the cited source lines myself, and reviewed every line of the diff.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Restore state after KV load rejection
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #49250.

When a synchronous external KV load is rejected under
`kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, scheduler state is rewound but Model
Runner V2 can retain the old device-side computed-token offset. With
overlapping batches, output already in flight can also mutate reset scheduler
state or be delivered after the request has been rescheduled. The result does
not match full recomputation.

This change:

- marks the exact in-flight token positions stale and clears speculative and
  placeholder state when a failed load is recomputed;
- propagates an explicit `rewound_req_ids` marker with cached-request data;
- applies the scheduler's absolute computed-token offset to Model Runner V2's
  device-side request state only for those explicit rollbacks; and
- adds focused scheduler and worker regression tests, including a multi-token
  speculative async frame.

There is no connector-specific special case.

This is materially different from #49252. That PR's scheduler fix derives a
frame count from `num_output_placeholders - 1` and explicitly scopes out
speculative decoding and diffusion. This change uses the existing exact
`num_in_flight_tokens` accounting and an explicit CPU-to-GPU rewind signal; it
was validated with EAGLE3. The difference was documented on #49250 before this
draft was opened.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py

ruff check \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py

ruff format --check \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py \
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

GPU negative-control protocol:

1. Run greedy decoding without a KV connector and record token IDs.
2. Use a connector that promises a block-aligned synchronous load and rejects
   it before copying KV.
3. Compare clean-base and patched output against the no-connector baseline for
   sync, async, and async EAGLE3 scheduling.
4. Repeat with real `LMCacheConnectorV1`, injecting a one-shot failure in a
   16-token retrieval before KV is copied.

## Test Result

- Focused tests: **16 passed**.
- Ruff check and format: **passed** for all five changed files.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Rebased cleanly onto `main` at `fe76112ff2`; focused tests and static checks
  were rerun after the final rebase.

Single-GPU negative control (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Model Runner V2 asserted,
greedy token-ID comparison):

| Configuration | Clean base | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Controlled rejection, sync | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Controlled rejection, async | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| EAGLE3 async, 2 draft tokens | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Real LMCache rejection, sync | differs from scratch | exact |
| Real LMCache rejection, async | differs from scratch | exact |

The sync, async, EAGLE3, and real-LMCache async smoke cases were rerun after the
preceding main rebase and remained exact. The final intervening upstream commit
only changes ROCm/DeepSeek files; the five files in this PR were unchanged.

Not covered: multi-GPU pipeline parallelism, hybrid KV cache manager, layerwise
LMCache loading, or multi-request shared-block recovery. A separate ordinary
LMCache-hit fused-layout corruption observed on this stack is outside this
change's scope; the forced-failure test rejects before any cached KV copy.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation,
implementation, and test orchestration. The human submitter reviewed all five
changed files, understands the change, and accepts maintenance responsibility.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV offload] Validate computed device pointers before copy
items.body:
## Problem

`compute_sub_block_ptrs()` in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py` derives raw
device addresses from `data_ptr()`, `stride(0)` and `shape[1]`:

```python
base_ptr = tensor.data_ptr()
row_stride = tensor.stride(0)
block_page_size = tensor.shape[1] // blocks_per_chunk
all_ptrs = (base_ptr + block_ids * row_stride) + sub_offsets
```

Those addresses are handed to the swap kernel, which dereferences them as
`int64*`:

```python
src = tl.load(src_addrs + job).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int64))
words = tl.load(sizes + job) // 8
data = tl.load(src + idx, mask=idx < words, other=0)
```

The `mask` bounds the copy against the *declared* size, not against the
allocation, and nothing validates the pointers themselves. The arithmetic
assumes a flat, unpadded row layout; a cache whose pages carry alignment
padding produces addresses that walk off the buffer.

### Reproduction

Enabling `OffloadingConnector` with a `fs_python` tier on DeepSeek-V4, whose MLA
pages are padded to 576B (`fp8_ds_mla`) or 584B, kills the worker during
startup:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access
was encountered'
```

Reproduced on v0.27.1 with and without the b12x attention backend, so it is not
backend-specific.

An IMA is the *lucky* outcome. Because the kernel masks against the declared
size rather than the allocation, the same mismatch can instead copy the wrong
bytes successfully and corrupt KV silently.

## Change

Adds a host-side bounds check on the computed pointer array, on both exit paths
of `compute_sub_block_ptrs()`. One `min`/`max` over the array per batch, which
is negligible next to the transfer itself.

On violation it raises a `ValueError` naming the offending range, the tensor
shape, dtype and `stride(0)`, and points at the likely cause, instead of
faulting inside the kernel.

## Scope

This does **not** add MLA/padded-page support to the offload path. It makes the
unsupported case fail diagnosably rather than dangerously. Supporting padded
layouts would additionally require deriving per-block offsets from
`MLAAttentionSpec.page_size_bytes`/`alignment` rather than `tensor.shape[1]`,
and handling multiple KV cache groups with differing geometry.

## Test

Logic verified for in-bounds, out-of-bounds and empty pointer arrays. Happy to
add a unit test under `tests/v1/kv_offload/` if you would like it in this PR;
I did not want to guess at the preferred fixture style.

items.body:
## Summary

- Carry each NIXL region's stride, block capacity, block size, cache-group mapping, and name through metadata exchange and descriptor construction.
- Register packed cache storage without collapsing independently sized regions.
- Pair regions deterministically and support pure-MLA peers whose P/D region layouts differ.

This is the generic geometry prerequisite needed before HiSparse can transfer long-context host regions safely.

## Duplicate check

#50717 is a draft limited to packed-cache block-size synchronization. #51527 is a draft targeting heterogeneous P/D logical block sizes. Neither provides the general per-region metadata, packed registration, group mapping, and descriptor geometry in this PR. The HiSparse stack needs that common substrate independently.

## Tests

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py -q
python -m pytest   tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py   tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py   tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py   -m cpu_test -q
```
